title: Doggish Through and Through | The Tale of the Demon Cat
subtitle: I am a cat in dog’s clothing, in every sense. This is my autobiography.
body:
## I In the autumn of the sixth year of Qingyuan, Demon Cat said goodbye to Cat Dad and Cat Mom, crossed distant seas, and went alone to the Ninth Heaven. “The mountains are high and the waters far. Be mindful of everything, stay composed, and do not panic. Remember, remember: do not learn human speech.” Cat Dad spoke earnestly; Demon Mom’s eyes brimmed with tears. Demon Cat nodded her agreement, but did not take it to heart. Human language made Demon Cat a little curious, but not curious enough to get herself killed. She had only heard the grown-up cats around her say that some cat children who went to the Ninth Heaven were taught human speech, intentionally or otherwise, by someone unknown. They forgot the language of cats, forgot their identity as cats, and forgot the way home. “I know! Don’t learn human talk. Human talk corrupts cats!” Demon Cat stuck out her tongue and spoke loudly to her parents in pure, authentic meow-speech. Suddenly Cat Mom caught her mischievous, tooth-baring grin, tugged her ear, and reproachfully licked the obedient little tuft on her head. Demon Cat playfully swept her tail twice across her parents’ whiskers and, under their expectant and worried gazes, leaped onto the divine tree that reached the Ninth Heaven.
## II The Ninth Heaven was a very boring place. Demon Cat discovered this in her first month there. There was no tasty cat food. Everything tasted like dog food. It was hard not to suspect that all the grown-up cats in the Ninth Heaven were dogs in disguise. A sign might clearly show little dried fish, yet stepping inside she would smell a heavy odor of bones. She was not so picky that she looked malnourished, but she secretly suspected that if she kept eating this way, she would soon become doggish through and through, inside and out. Her suspicions were not unfounded. Last week, while eating with a black-cat friend who had arrived in the Ninth Heaven before her, Demon Cat expertly slurped beef in sour broth into her mouth. Her friend’s eyes nearly popped out. “My goodness, why do you eat like a dog, picking nothing out and shoving everything into your mouth? You can eat the beef, but the pickled greens and broth are just for flavoring. Why eat those?” Demon Cat shrugged, pushed her emptied bowl toward the table’s edge, and stretched out a paw, licking it haphazardly. “A dog, then. I haven’t had cat food in ages. My stomach won’t let me waste anything. It would cry.” As she spoke, she quite naturally reached out and pushed the bowl, already at the edge, a little farther. Black Cat looked at the wooden bowl wobbling on the floor, still trying to spin, and shook her head. “You should learn to cook some cat food yourself. Stop going to dog restaurants all day. Dog food is fast food; cats get malnourished eating too much of it.” Demon Cat stretched, jumped down, and picked up the bowl. “I tried learning, but learned absolutely nothing. First I broke the bowl, then burned through the pot, then upset my stomach. Even with nine lives I couldn’t survive the repeated trials of my genius for disastrous cooking. Besides, I’m not a nine-tailed cat. Cooking takes talent, and my talent in the opposite direction is far too outstanding. Better not waste the Ninth Heaven’s grains and vegetables.” “Then come eat at my place over summer break. You can’t keep eating dog food day after day.” Black Cat shook her head and served Demon Cat another bowl of fish soup. ## III I forgot to mention: Demon Cat had come to the Ninth Heaven to learn the art of dragon slaying. What dragons had done wrong to deserve being slaughtered in so many different ways, Demon Cat did not know. Why she had to learn seventy-two methods of killing them, she did not quite understand either. As for what dragons looked like, their daily routines, their likes and dislikes, she knew absolutely nothing. She could not even be sure that dragons existed. Why had she started thinking about all these dragon-slaying questions? That goes back to the month before last, when her master, Snake Six, once again told her to spend summer washing dishes and carrying plates at Five-Spice Hall. “Demon Cat, go help Lord Rabbit Two at Five-Spice Hall this summer and refine your dragon-slaying banquet skills.” Demon Cat wrinkled her nose. “But Master, I’ve already worked there for four years.” “Didn’t your senior fellow disciple Dog Two work there for three years? Why can’t you go refine your skills some more?” “But all the friends who enrolled with me are practicing actual dragon-slaying moves. I’m the only one carrying plates at Five-Spice Hall every year.” “No buts! Do you want your master to expel you!” “N-no…” Demon Cat did not want to talk back. But the work at Five-Spice Hall was hard and exhausting. By the end of each day, she was too tired to think about cultivating her inner dragon-slaying skills. Watching her friends practice with growing competence, she felt troubled and envious. ## IV “So annoying. Lord Cha Two at Meta keeps making me grind fish into powder, shape the powder back into fish, then grind it into powder, shape it into fish…” “I’m annoyed too. Five-Spice Hall is desperately short-staffed. I have to carry plates and wash dishes. Most outrageous of all, when a pot breaks or the stove leaks, they make me fix those too.” Black Cat and Demon Cat sat side by side on the roof of Five-Spice Hall. The fragrance of food drifted up, but neither had much appetite. “Want to get some bug water?” Demon Cat ventured. “Bug water is too boring. Let’s try the mint juice at that new place. I hear Granny Grass from the divine tree asked her squirrel granddaughter to carry it up to the Ninth Heaven. It should taste like the cat-grass cheese drink we had as kittens.” Black Cat deftly put on her bamboo-copter and leaped off Five-Spice Hall in one bound. At Kung Fu Cat Café, Demon Cat stared blankly as Black Cat took a pair of chopsticks from inside her clothes. “Why do you carry those around???” Black Cat shrugged, her smile restrainedly unrestrained. “You never know.” Indeed: the two cats who had meant to go slurp mint water had wound their way into a nearby shop selling dog-made flatbread. And indeed, after Black Cat worked on it, the big dogs’ flatbread tasted to Demon Cat a little like a cat-style wrap. You never know. Black Cat had not lied to her. ## To Be Continued ## An Unreasonable Prediction: This Will Be My Longest-Running Writing Project Chapters 1–3 were written on March 11, 2023, on the little Amtrak train home from DC. Chapter 4 was an update promised to a friend after whale watching. I updated this on March 30 after returning from a boat trip out of Half Moon Bay. It’s a little short. Please don’t mind.
